details: The US Senate passed a resolution to curb presidential military actions against Iran, though a presidential veto is anticipated. Simultaneously, negotiations continue between the US and Iran aimed at a broader peace framework. These discussions encompass sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program, and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. A temporary waiver on oil sanctions has allowed Iran to sell oil in dollars, leading to a drop in crude oil prices.
title: US Senate Votes on Iran War Powers; Peace Talks Progress

details: An analyst suggests that the Strait of Hormuz will not revert to its pre-war status, as Iran and Oman are moving towards joint administration, imposing transit fees, and restricting hazardous military use. This development is linked to the ongoing US-Iran talks.
title: Iran and Oman to Administer Strait of Hormuz

details: For the first time, a Taliban delegation held talks with the European Union in Brussels. The discussions focused on diplomatic services and the return of Afghan migrants in Europe. The meeting has drawn strong criticism from human rights organizations.
title: EU Hosts Taliban Delegation Amidst Criticism

details: Global stock markets, particularly the tech and semiconductor sectors, experienced a notable sell-off on June 23, 2026. This downturn was attributed to profit-taking, concerns over increasing debt-funded AI spending, and the anticipation of more aggressive interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve. Major indices like South Korea's KOSPI plunged by 10%, and the Nasdaq fell by 2.2%.
title: Global Tech Stocks See Significant Sell-off

details: President Trump signed an Executive Order on June 22, 2026, to accelerate the federal government's adoption of post-quantum cryptography. This initiative aims to protect sensitive data and critical infrastructure from future advanced cryptographic attacks by quantum computers, with deadlines set for federal agencies and contractors to transition their systems.
title: US Executive Order on Post-Quantum Cryptography

details: The European Union acknowledges the increasing exploitation of cryptocurrencies by criminals in illicit trafficking. To counter this, the EU is backing the development of advanced technologies, including blockchain analytics, to aid law enforcement in combating such activities.
sourceName: European Commission, Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs
title: EU Targets Cryptocurrency Use in Illicit Trafficking
